intended_object: The radius of the circle in the q-disc that is the image, under q = e^{2πiτ}, of the horizontal line Im τ = H. That radius is |q| = e^{-2πH}. This comes from the docstring and from the use in Seg5CuspIntegral.lean, where qParam 1 of the top boundary segment is shown to equal circleMap 0 (seg5QRadiusH H) (…).
explanation: The body is exactly `Real.exp (-2 * π * H)`. This equals ‖exp(2πiτ)‖ when Im τ = H, which is ‖Function.Periodic.qParam 1 τ‖. So it is the correct q-expansion radius, with period 1, at height H. It is a specific explicit real number that depends on H, so it is not too narrow just because it is specific. One could ask for a general period h, which would give e^{-2πH/h}. But this library only works with level 1 (period 1) for the valence formula, where the cusp width is 1, so that is the setting the definition needs. Mathlib has no separate named definition for this radius. It only has `Function.Periodic.qParam` and lemmas about its norm.
